evidence.detail: Exact v308 rs/C, the AWT applet/input base, constructs exactly one rs/m/a and writes mouse press/release/move and wheel events into it while input buffering is enabled.
Keyboard handlers in rs/C update separate key-state structures and do not enqueue into rs/m/a, proving this buffer is mouse-input specific rather than a generic client input queue.
The class owns a fixed 256-entry rs/m/a$a ring, synchronized enqueue/drain/reset methods, read/write cursor state and an overflow counter.
Type-3 events are coalesced with the newest pending type-3 record: current x/y/time are updated while min/max x/y bounds are widened, matching batched mouse-motion semantics.

Client drains buffered rs/m/a$a records each cycle, updates mouse coordinates/button state from event types 1/2/3, handles type 5 as wheel input, and uses type 4 as the reset/fence marker emitted by the buffer.

proposals.note: Descriptive exact-v308 name for the synchronized 256-entry AWT mouse event ring consumed by Client.

evidence.detail: Each record stores event type, button/wheel value, x/y, min/max x/y and event timestamp; constructor/reset logic initializes current and min/max coordinates together.
The only owning collection is R353 MouseInputEventBuffer, which preallocates 256 records and copies them into Client's drain array.
Client interprets the record type discriminator as mouse press/release/move/fence/wheel behavior and consumes the timestamp plus coordinate/button fields directly.

proposals.note: Descriptive exact-v308 name for one buffered mouse input record.
